value: Building leases are governed by the Act on Land and Building Leases (借地借家法, Act No. 90 of 1991) and by the lease provisions of the Civil Code (民法, Act No. 89 of 1896).
note: Act on Land and Building Leases (Act No. 90 of 1991, 借地借家法), Japanese text read on e-Gov through its official data API; the Japanese text prevails.

value: A landlord who has received a deposit (敷金, whatever it is called) must return the balance after deducting the tenant's unpaid money obligations when the lease has ended and the property is returned, or when the tenant lawfully assigns the lease; the landlord may apply it to unpaid debts, but the tenant may not demand that it be used for them (Civil Code Art. 622-2). The law sets no cap on the amount.
note: Civil Code (Act No. 89 of 1896, 民法), Japanese text read on e-Gov through its official data API; the Japanese text prevails.

value: Unless agreed otherwise, rent for buildings is payable at the end of each month (Civil Code Art. 614).
note: Civil Code (Act No. 89 of 1896, 民法), Japanese text read on e-Gov through its official data API; the Japanese text prevails.

value: Either party may claim an increase or decrease of building rent for the future if it has become unreasonable because of changes in taxes or other burdens, in land or building prices or economic conditions, or in comparison with similar buildings, regardless of the contract terms (Art. 32). A clause that rent will not be increased for a set period prevails. The Act sets no fixed percentage cap.
note: Act on Land and Building Leases (Act No. 90 of 1991, 借地借家法), Japanese text read on e-Gov through its official data API; the Japanese text prevails.

value: A building lease with a fixed term of less than one year is treated as a lease without a fixed term (Art. 29(1)). The 50-year maximum term of the Civil Code does not apply to building leases (Art. 29(2)).
note: Act on Land and Building Leases (Act No. 90 of 1991, 借地借家法), Japanese text read on e-Gov through its official data API; the Japanese text prevails.

value: If neither party gives notice of non-renewal (or notice of a change of terms) between one year and six months before the end of a fixed term, the lease is deemed renewed on the same terms, with no fixed term (Art. 26(1)); the same applies if the tenant stays on after expiry and the landlord does not object without delay (Art. 26(2)).
note: Act on Land and Building Leases (Act No. 90 of 1991, 借地借家法), Japanese text read on e-Gov through its official data API; the Japanese text prevails.

value: When the landlord gives notice of termination, the lease ends six months after the notice (Art. 27(1)); a landlord's notice of non-renewal or termination is valid only if there is just cause, judged on the needs of both parties, the history of the lease, how the building is used, its condition and any payment offered for moving out (Art. 28).
note: Act on Land and Building Leases (Act No. 90 of 1991, 借地借家法), Japanese text read on e-Gov through its official data API; the Japanese text prevails.

value: For a lease with no fixed term, each party may give notice of termination at any time, and a building lease ends three months after the notice (Civil Code Art. 617(1)(ii)).
note: Civil Code (Act No. 89 of 1896, 民法), Japanese text read on e-Gov through its official data API; the Japanese text prevails.

value: A fixed-term building lease that is not renewable can be made only in writing (for example a notarial deed, or an electronic record treated as writing), and the landlord must first give the tenant a separate written explanation that there is no renewal (Art. 38(1)-(3)).
note: Act on Land and Building Leases (Act No. 90 of 1991, 借地借家法), Japanese text read on e-Gov through its official data API; the Japanese text prevails.
